(Detroit, Michigan) | college = [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]] (2016–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]] | team1 = [[Motor City Cruise]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = [[Grand Rapids Gold]] | years3 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]]–2024 | team3 = [[Club Ourense Baloncesto|Río Ourense Termal]] | years4 = 2024–2025 | team4 = [[KK Włocławek|Anwil Włocławek]] | years5 = 2025 | team5 = [[KK Studentski centar|SC Derby]] | years6 = 2025–2026 | team6 = [[BC Gargždai]] | years7 = 2026–present | team7 = [[ASK Karditsas B.C.|Karditsa]] | highlights = *3x First-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2019-2021) *MAC All-Freshman Team (2018) }} '''Justin Rafael Turner''' (born March 12, 1998), nicknamed "'''Juice'''" or "'''JT'''", is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[ASK Karditsas B.C.|Karditsa]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green Falcons]]. ==Early life== Turner was born and grew up in [[Detroit, Michigan]], and attended [[Renaissance High School (Michigan)|Renaissance High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2019/01/18/ex-detroit-renaissance-star-justin-turner-has-bowling-green-falcons-rise/2615094002/|title=Ex-Detroit Renaissance star Justin Turner has Bowling Green on the rise|first=David|last=Goricki|work=[[The Detroit News]]|date=January 18, 2019|access-date=April 16, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 21 points, seven rebounds, and five assists per game and was named first team All-City and second team All-State.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/04/07/boys-basketball-detroit/82768514/|title=All-Detroit boys basketball teams|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=April 7, 2016|access-date=April 16, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://michiganpreps.rivals.com/news/justin-turner-stays-close-to-home-at-bowling-green|title=Justin Turner stays close to home, at Bowling Green|first=Branden|last=Hunter|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 12, 2016|access-date=April 16, 2020}} He committed to the [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green Falcons]] over several other [[Mid-American Conference]] schools. ==College career== Turner played in four games as a true freshman before using a medical [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] due to a season-ending injury. He was named to the [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) All-Freshman team and honorable mention all-conference after averaging 15.9 points per game as a redshirt freshman.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Justin-Turner-Bowling-Green-UConn-Arkansas-Xavier-Gonzaga-Cincinnati-Missouri-Alabama-Marquette-Louisville-Arizona-State-145302168/|title=Long list of schools after Bowling Green transfer Justin Turner|first=Evan|last=Daniels|website=247Sports.com|date=March 23, 2020|access-date=April 16, 2020}} Turner averaged 18.2 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.4 steals per game and was named first team All-MAC the following season.{{cite web|url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/bgsu/2019/11/02/180-is-magic-number-for-bowling-green-bgsu-justin-turner/stories/20191101132|title=180 is the magic number for BGSU's Justin Turner|first=Nicholas|last=Piotrowicz|work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]]|date=November 2, 2019|access-date=April 16, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2019/11/4/20937642/bowling-green-turner-huger-frye-falcons-mac-preview-buffalo-whitesell-toledo-rockets-basketball|title=Justin Turner and the Bowling Green Falcons look to cash in on big expectations in an open MAC|first=Greg|last=Mitchell|website=MidMajorMadness.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=November 4, 2019|access-date=April 16, 2020}} Turner scored his 1,000th career point on a late layup to help the Falcons to a 73–69 win over Akron on February 19, 2019, part of a 23-point performance.{{cite web|url=https://www.sent-trib.com/sports/turner-hits-game-winner-and-th-point/article_e11de6e0-34bf-11e9-998c-7732e67280c1.html|title=Turner hits game winner and 1,000th point|first=Jack|last=Carle|work=Sentinel-Tribune|date=February 19, 2019|access-date=April 17, 2020}} He initially declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but withdrew after working out for several teams, returning to Bowling Green for his redshirt junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/bgsu/2019/05/29/justin-turner-bgsu-bowling-green-basketball-nba-draft-return/stories/20190529160|title=Justin Turner reflects on NBA draft process, decision to return|first=Nicholas|last=Piotrowicz|work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]]|date=May 29, 2019|access-date=April 16, 2020}} Turner was named first team All-MAC for a second straight season after averaging 18.8 points, 4.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2020/04/02/bowling-green-graduate-transfer-justin-turner-has-marquette-list/5094649002/|title=Marquette has reached out to several transfer players, including Bowling Green's Justin Turner|first=Ben|last=Steele|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=April 2, 2020|access-date=April 16, 2020}} After the season Turner entered the transfer portal and was widely considered to be one of the best graduate transfer players available.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Justin-Turner-Bowling-Green-Missouri-Xavier-Marquette-Arkansas-Louisville-Iowa-State-145430580/|title=Graduate transfer Justin Turner cuts his list to six|first=Evan|last=Daniels|website=247Sports.com|date=March 27, 2020|access-date=April 16, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_mens_basketball/prized-transfer-target-justin-turner-has-missouri-in-final-four-as-decision-looms/article_e7bb0bde-775a-11ea-9af0-87d9ab38ee8c.html|title=Prized transfer target Justin Turner has Missouri in final four as decision looms|work=[[Columbia Missourian]]|date=April 5, 2020|access-date=April 16, 2020}} Turner ultimately decided to return to Bowling Green for his redshirt senior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29030518/justin-turner-opts-stay-bowling-green-rather-transfer|title=Justin Turner opts to stay at Bowling Green rather than transfer|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=April 13, 2020|access-date=April 16, 2020}} On February 16, 2021, Turner became the first player in school history to surpass the 2,000 career point mark.{{cite news|url= https://bgsufalcons.com/news/2021/2/16/mens-basketball-huger-wins-100th-game-turner-nets-2-000th-point-in-bgsus-victory-at-ball-state.aspx |title= Huger Wins 100th Game & Turner Nets 2,000th Point In BGSU's Victory At Ball State |publisher=[[Bowling Green Falcons]]|date=February 16, 2021|access-date=February 17, 2021}} He averaged 19.3 points and 4.4 assist per game as a redshirt senior.{{cite news |last1=Rowland |first1=Kyle |title=Toledo men's basketball continues racking up awards |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2021/03/16/Toledo-men-s-basketball-continues-racking-up-awards/stories/20210316119 |access-date=June 17, 2021 |work=[[Toledo Blade]] |date=March 16, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Motor City Cruise (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Turner played for the San Antonio Spurs in the [[2021 NBA Summer League]]. Turner made his debut in an 87–58 loss against the [[Utah Jazz]]'s "White" Team on August 3. He led the team with 13 points and seven rebounds along with one assist, steal, and block.{{Cite web|title=San Antonio vs. Utah - Game Summary - August 3, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-summer/game/_/gameId/401352126|access-date=2021-08-10|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} On October 23, 2021, the [[Westchester Knicks]] selected Turner with their fourth overall pick in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]].{{cite web|title=Delaware Blue Coats Select Shamorie Ponds With First Pick Of 2021-22 NBA G League Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/delaware-blue-coats-select-shamorie-ponds-with-first-pick-of-2021-22-nba-g-league-draft|date=October 23, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 25, 2021, Turner was included in training camp roster of the [[Westchester Knicks]],{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-training-camp-roster|date=October 25, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 25, 2021}} but was waived before the season began. On November 15, he signed with the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite web|title=MOTOR CITY CRUISE CLAIM JUSTIN TURNER OFF WAIVERS|url=https://detroit.gleague.nba.com/news/motor-city-cruise-claim-justin-turner-off-waivers/|website=NBA.com|date=November 15, 2021|access-date=November 15, 2021}} ===Grand Rapids Gold (2023)=== On March 2, 2023, Turner was acquired by the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/grand-rapids-gold-acquire-justin-turner-from-available-player-pool/n-5930089|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Grand Rapids Gold Acquire Justin Turner from Available Player Pool|date=March 2, 2023|access-date=March 2, 2023}} ===Río Ourense Termal (2023–2024)=== On July 5, 2023, Turner signed with [[Club Ourense Baloncesto|Río Ourense Termal]] of the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]].{{cite web|title=Tras una larga negociación Justin Turner se convierte en el cuarto jugador del Club Ourense Baloncesto 2023-2024|url=https://www.clubourensebaloncesto.com/index.php?lm=2758|website=ClubOurenseBaloncesto.com|date=July 5, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023|language=Spanish}} ===Anwil Włocławek (2024–2025)=== On July 7, 2024, he signed with [[KK Włocławek|Anwil Włocławek]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] (PLK).{{Cite web|url=https://plk.pl/aktualnosci/24745/justin-turner-w-anwilu|title=Justin Turner w Anwilu|last=|first=|date=July 7, 2024|website=plk.pl|publisher=|language=pl|access-date=July 8, 2024}} ===Gargždai (2025–2026)=== On December 22, 2025, Turner signed with [[BC Gargždai]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL).{{Cite web|url=https://gargzdaibasketball.lt/justin-turner-prisijungia-prie-gargzdu-krepsinio-klubo/|title=Justin Turner prisijungia prie Gargždų krepšinio klubo|last=|first=|date=December 22, 2025|website=gargzdaibasketball.lt|publisher=|language=lt|access-date=December 29, 2025}} ===Karditsa (2026–present)=== On July 1, 2026, Turner signed with [[ASK Karditsas B.C.|Karditsa]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.askarditsas.gr/me-ton-tzastin-terner-enischyetai-o-a-s-karditsas-iaponiki/|title=Με τον
